RESEARCH / EXOPLANET ATMOSPHERES01
Radiative balance · conceptual illustration
NAOJ · JAN 2025–AUG 20262026

When can a cloud survive?

Modeling how eight cloud-forming materials absorb starlight and cool. First-author research on what keeps clouds stable in exoplanet atmospheres, with Kazumasa Ohno.

Read the paper ↗GitHub ↗
Behind the research+

A particle can be hotter or cooler than the gas around it. The model explores how composition, particle size, and stellar radiation shape that difference—and whether a cloud can remain stable.

T. M. Shefferson-Nagata & K. Ohno (2026). Radiatively Controlled Thermal Stability of High-altitude Clouds in Exoplanetary Atmospheres. ApJ 1005, 210.

The repository contains a partial reconstruction of the research scripts; it is not a complete reproducibility release.

FOUNDER · AUG 2023–MAR 2026AI / EDUCATION

NOBILVA

An AI learning companion for children facing barriers to attending school. I built the product and grew a 17-person team, supporting more than 150 students across Japan.

More about the project+

The project received Japanese government grant funding and institutional support, and won the national Grand Prize at the Japan AI Education Utilization Award, among 477 teams.

03 /THE PERSON BEHIND THE PROJECTS

A little more human.

I like moving between worlds: abstract mathematics and messy problems, the sky above us and the things right in front of us.

Outside research, you’ll find me watching films, playing guitar, running, or on a badminton court. At Princeton, I’m involved in Quantitative Traders, Student Ventures, and the Robotics Club, where we’re building a BB-8 droid.

I work in Japanese and English. Always happy to trade ideas across disciplines.
